blogs.title: Autoimmune HIT: Beyond Classic Heparin-Dependent Antibodies
blogs.description: An exploration of autoimmune HIT (aHIT) as a distinct entity from classic HIT, focusing on the pathophysiology of heparin-independent platelet-activating antibodies. This post will discuss how aHIT can explain unusually severe clinical courses, profound thrombocytopenia, and delayed platelet count recovery—and why clinicians need to maintain a high index of suspicion for this under-recognized variant.
blogs.title: Early-Onset HIT: The Preoperative Heparin Connection
blogs.description: A deep dive into the timing of HIT onset after cardiac surgery, contrasting the typical POD5-10 window with early-onset cases before POD5. This post will explain how preoperative heparin exposure (in this case, during cardiac catheterization) can 'prime the clock' for earlier HIT presentation, and how this knowledge can prevent clinicians from incorrectly ruling out HIT based on temporal assumptions.
blogs.title: Decoding the Indeterminate SRA: A Novel Serological Profile
blogs.description: A case-based discussion of the serotonin-release assay (SRA) interpretation challenges, focusing on this patient's unique profile showing partial resistance to Fc receptor blockade (IV.3 monoclonal antibody). This post will help clinicians understand why 'indeterminate' results shouldn't automatically exclude HIT, and how atypical lab patterns may signal autoimmune HIT.
blogs.title: Severe aHIT: When Argatroban Isn't Enough
blogs.description: A practical guide to escalating therapy in refractory autoimmune HIT, including the role of high-dose IVIG (and expected platelet count responses), considerations for switching from argatroban to fondaparinux, and the utility of monitoring fibrinogen, D-dimer, and schistocytes to gauge control of HIT-associated hypercoagulability. Special attention to antithrombin supplementation when transitioning to fondaparinux.
blogs.title: HIT-Induced Consumptive Coagulopathy: Reading the Danger Signs
blogs.description: An analysis of severe HIT as a consumptive coagulopathy, examining how falling fibrinogen, rising D-dimer, and schistocyte appearance signal uncontrolled hypercoagulability. This post will discuss why these markers matter beyond platelet counts and how they can guide therapeutic decisions, including when to escalate or change anticoagulation strategies.
